title: HE WAS JUST PASSING BY.
paragraphs: HE WAS JUST PASSING BY.

No plan.
No warning.
No idea his name would echo through eternity.
Mark tells it in one line:
“A certain man from Cyrene, Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and they forced him to carry the cross.” — Gospel of Mark 15:21
Passing by.
That’s it.

Simon wasn’t a disciple.
He wasn’t a volunteer.
He wasn’t part of the crowd screaming for blood.
He was just walking into the city.
Then Rome grabbed him.

A soldier’s hand on his shoulder.
A command barked in a language that meant you don’t argue.
“Carry it.”
And suddenly Simon’s hands were on the wood meant for Jesus.
The Weight of Someone Else’s Sentence
Picture it.

The beam rough against his skin.
Splinters biting into his palms.
The smell of sweat, blood, and dust in the Jerusalem air.
And beside him—
Jesus.

Bruised.
Bleeding.
Barely standing.
Simon didn’t know the full story yet.
But he felt the weight.
Not just wood.

Judgment.
Sin.
History itself.
The cross pressed into his shoulder while the Son of God staggered beside him.
And the road to Golgotha suddenly had two men carrying one cross.
Here’s the twist.
Simon thought Rome forced him.
But heaven was writing a different script.
Because Jesus had already said:
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.” — Gospel of Mark 8:34
Simon didn’t volunteer.
Yet he became the first man in history to literally do it.
And something changed that day.
Mark drops a small detail like a quiet thunderclap:
Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
Why mention them?
Many scholars believe the early church knew these men personally.
Which means this moment didn’t end on the road to Golgotha.
It followed Simon home.

Around the dinner table.
Into the hearts of his sons.
Into the story of the church.
A man who met Jesus under the weight of the cross raised sons who followed Him.
Listen closely.
Sometimes you think you’re just passing through life.

Just another day.
Just another crowd.
Just another moment.
Then suddenly—
God interrupts your path with a cross.

Pain.
Responsibility.
A burden you didn’t choose.
And you think:
Why me?

But what if the place where the cross touches your shoulder
is the place where you finally walk beside Jesus?
Because here’s the Gospel.
Simon carried the wood.
Jesus carried the sin.
Simon helped for a moment.
Jesus finished the work forever.

At Golgotha, Christ took the full weight—
your rebellion,
your shame,
your hidden failures—
and nailed them to the cross.
Not partially.
Completely.
And three days later, death lost the argument.
So if today you feel like life forced something onto your shoulders…
Look again.
You may not just be passing by.
You might be walking closer to Jesus than you ever have.
🔥 Friend, the cross you carry might be the place you meet the Savior.
And if you’ve never trusted Him—
Today is the day.

Lay your sin down.
Trust the One who carried it all the way to the grave—and walked out alive.
Because Jesus doesn’t just change history.
He rewrites lives.
✝️ We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
